body:
## Canonical private-launch checkpoint — 11 September 2026

**Start implementation with #274's remaining caller and administration-contract cleanup.** The first release remains private and single-owner; #269 stays deferred outside launch dependencies. The accepted product specification below is unchanged.

Main `e4d49f420e9cb3c0343ef54a9948720aadbdf146` (PR #304), schema 32: [current-main CI 34552632337](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/actions/runs/34552632337) passes all nine required jobs. Routine validation is green; extended journeys, full stress, accepted-tier capacity and live rollout remain separate evidence gates.

The original implementation slices #217–#235 are closed; #233 explicitly transferred unfinished capacity/fault criteria into #268. The merged #284 integration and #299/#300 testing improvements, #302 toolchain update and #304 maintenance supersede the old September 9 wave list. Source/parser/identity/publication structure must not be rebuilt from stale checkpoints.

### Completed ticket reconciliation

- [x] #271 — routine validation restored, with exact current-main CI; full stress/extended/capacity evidence remains separate.
- [x] #272 — preserved Worker toolchain reconciled and integrated; old patch remains archived.
- [x] #273 — realistic streamed fixtures and source/storage accounting; no accepted-tier capacity certification.
- [x] #301 — pnpm/Corepack adoption and the specified Vite+ fallback; Vite+ adoption is not claimed.
- [x] #303 — typed ESLint/Prettier evaluation, followed by separately authorized implementation/removal now integrated through #304.

Current setup is Node 26.8.2 / Corepack 0.36.0 / pnpm 12.3.4, TS7 compilation with TS6 tooling API, ESLint and Prettier, six compiler projects and shared workflow setup. Maintained interfaces are in `contracts/`. The documented editor imported-type refresh limitation remains.

### Next work and execution order

| Order/lane | Tickets | Actual remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First implementation | #274 | Four full-stress success callers still invoke retired run approval; maintained administration docs still advertise the old path. Finish native callers/contracts, retain intentional historical replay and actual restore, and validate. |
| Proof after the caller fix | #253, #275, #276 | Complete current full stress, design/prove bounded workload segmentation and accounting before large tiers, map existing durable faults and fill gaps, and run required extended recovery/real-source journeys explicitly. |
| Release preparation alongside it | #236 / draft PR #246 | Reconcile the conflicted existing draft, replace Node 22/npm setup with current shared tooling, preserve exact-version/isolation behavior, and prepare account/credential and fresh capacity prerequisites. |
| Scheduled-source evidence | #267 | Reviewed implementation/manual proof is integrated; actual default-branch scheduled success remains. A manual run is not scheduled proof. |
| Release execution | #236 → #237 → #238; #239 | Actual isolated dev, manual exact-commit staging, automatic same-commit production through fresh guards; revalidate/release the existing pre-fold handoff after relevant schema changes. |
| Final convergence | #268 → #240; #151; #136 | Reconcile combined capacity/fault results, complete each enabled game's required journeys and rollout/handoff proof, then regenerate final freeze and obtain the separate Go-Live declaration. |

#274 is dependency-ready. #253's complete stress run depends on its caller migration. After completed-provider closure, #275/#276/#239 retain #274 as a real open dependency; their bounded design/audit work may begin before final integrated execution. Keep heavy runtime tests and measurements serial on one host. Preserve historical dependency edges and refresh current-main evidence at each implementation boundary.

### Proof boundaries and human decisions

The green default stress run covers two bounded tests, not the ten-file full selection or accepted tiers. The fixture graph has 20,625 / 206,250 requests against a 5,000 fixture policy and 25,000 emergency ceiling; #275 must prove a supported arrangement rather than equate guard rejection with usable capacity. One Piece P-001 is a bounded scope; Riftbound's retained census includes missing image bytes and an unexplained metadata count difference. Keep all scope/measurement limitations explicit.

`test:full` is routine regression coverage. Extended `composed-recovery`, `one-piece-two-source` and `riftbound-catalogue`, benchmarks, full stress and live rollout are distinct evidence. Preserve tested SHAs, historical failures, actual SQL restore and exact-release-SHA gates.

The dev account/credential-isolation choice, fresh capacity/replacement headroom, actual first installation/rollout and #239 live handoff remain operational prerequisites. Offline code work continues independently. Final Go-Live is a separate explicit owner decision after technical completion. No live operation is authorized merely by updating this tracker.

Evidence: [current maintenance baseline](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/blob/e4d49f420e9cb3c0343ef54a9948720aadbdf146/docs/evidence/repo-maintenance-20260911.md), [testing policy](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/blob/e4d49f420e9cb3c0343ef54a9948720aadbdf146/docs/testing.md), [toolchain](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/blob/e4d49f420e9cb3c0343ef54a9948720aadbdf146/docs/toolchain.md). Each child now records its concrete next step and scope. Historical failed-run and provider checkpoints in comments remain attributable to their original code.

## Problem Statement

The owner needs one trustworthy private catalogue for applications that reference real Cards and individual Printings across publishers. Existing Bandai-only, official-source-only contracts cannot represent supplemental-only Printings, source-independent identity or differing publisher semantics reliably. The reviewed implementation also has reproduced real-data defects and catalogue-size limits, while the current approval surface cannot expose every proposed change.

Before Catalogue Consumers depend on the API, the service needs realistic evidence of correctness and capacity, isolated dev/staging/production environments, and a deliberate release path. Closing planning issues or passing synthetic tests alone is not proof that real catalogues can be inspected, published, consumed and recovered.

## Solution

Evolve Card Keepr into an English-language, private, single-owner catalogue with source-specific adapters into shared Game Profiles, permanent canonical identities, auditable supplemental/manual admission and owner-designated authority. Publish accepted card content and explicit unknowns through a consistent API and immutable Catalogue Exports; keep evidence and source health in administration. Exclude tournament eligibility, ban lists, FAQs and rulings while retaining Printed Rules Text and publisher-issued corrections.

Collect evidence concurrently, prepare and review immutable candidates independently per game through bounded durable operations, and atomically publish a consistent composition with a verified-backup checkpoint between publications. Validate One Piece against Bandai and Limitless, actual Riftbound data, and every additional game before enabling it for consumers.

Automatically deploy passing merges to dev. The owner manually starts a release attempt for an exact commit in staging; successful staging validation leads automatically to production promotion of that same commit through rechecked production guards. Software promotion and Catalogue publication are separate: production facts still require production Catalogue Candidate inspection and approval.

## User Stories

1. As the owner, I want Supported Games from different Publishers, so that my applications do not need separate catalogue conventions per publisher.
2. As the owner, I want English editions modelled separately from release regions, so that source geography does not invent a language or edition.
3. As the owner, I want several Sources for one game, so that one catalogue's omissions do not define the available Cards and Printings.
4. As the owner, I want Official Source to mean publisher-owned, so that supplemental evidence is never misrepresented as official.
5. As the owner, I want to designate Source Authority for card facts, printing details and corrected content, so that games without usable official catalogues remain supportable.
6. As the owner, I want an authority change to require an explicit decision, so that a newly available official source cannot silently replace my selected policy.
7. As the owner, I want each source adapter to map into the game's shared Game Profile, so that source presentation cannot redefine game semantics.
8. As the owner, I want Game Profiles to evolve deliberately, so that new mechanics and changed meanings are represented accurately.
9. As the owner, I want unknown optional source fields preserved with warnings, so that harmless publisher additions do not discard evidence or break a refresh.
10. As the owner, I want required structure and identity failures to remain blocking, so that warning tolerance does not admit invalid records.
11. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want stable opaque Card IDs, so that publisher numbering and source URL changes do not break my references.
12. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want stable opaque Printing IDs, so that applications can reference individual issued variants.
13. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want game-specific Card equivalence, so that similar rules or numbering do not incorrectly collapse distinct game pieces.
14. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want distinct issued artwork, treatment, stamps, printed content and faces represented as Printings, so that meaningful physical variants stay addressable.
15. As the owner, I want attributable source-record mappings, so that the same Printing can be recognised across independent source identifiers.
16. As the owner, I want ambiguous matches held for review, so that names, numbers or image similarity alone cannot merge records.
17. As the owner, I want to admit real unnumbered cards, so that missing publisher numbers do not force fabricated identifiers.
18. As the owner, I want explicit merge and split corrections, so that mistakes can be repaired without silently reassigning published IDs.
19. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want redirects and replacement relationships for identity corrections, so that I can reconcile references and choose between split variants myself.
20. As the owner, I want identity mappings and correction history recoverable, so that restoration preserves consumer references.
21. As the owner, I want supplemental sources to introduce new Cards and Printings, so that their contribution is not restricted to enriching existing entities.
22. As the owner, I want manual real-card intake, so that I can fill a gap when ordinary ingestion does not supply the record.
23. As the owner, I want admission requirements appropriate to each game and source, so that evidence standards remain useful without a universal two-source checklist.
24. As the owner, I want permitted authoritative sources to admit unambiguous records automatically, so that routine intake does not require repeated manual decisions.
25. As the owner, I want unresolved Entity Proposals kept outside published data, so that incomplete evidence can be investigated without speculative duplicates.
26. As the owner, I want to admit, link, reject and reconsider Entity Proposals with history, so that decisions remain explainable when evidence changes.
27. As the owner, I want explicit evidence-backed admission exceptions, including my recorded inspection, so that unusual real cards can be represented without disguising uncertainty.
28. As the owner, I want Curated Revisions for established facts, so that corrections remain distinct from new-entity intake.
29. As the owner, I want material source changes to prompt reaffirmation of overrides, so that old corrections cannot silently override newly relevant evidence.
30. As the owner, I want later publisher confirmation attached to existing identities, so that supplemental records do not acquire duplicate IDs.
31. As the owner, I want conflicts resolved through declared authority, so that recency, publisher ownership and arbitrary trust scores do not decide truth.
32. As the owner, I want unresolved problems isolated where consistency permits, so that one unresolved proposal need not block unrelated facts.
33. As the owner, I want exclusions exposed during review, so that isolation never becomes silent data loss.
34. As the owner, I want refresh scopes declared by Source, locale and supported subset, so that I can refresh one set or source without pretending to check everything.
35. As the owner, I want required and optional source participation fixed before collection, so that an outage cannot silently weaken the plan.
36. As the owner, I want partial required capture to block publication, so that 99 successful pages are not presented as complete coverage of 100.
37. As the owner, I want an explicit independently complete narrower retry, so that useful retained evidence can support a deliberately smaller refresh.
38. As the owner, I want optional-source outages to carry accepted facts forward truthfully, so that source downtime does not remove valid catalogue records.
39. As the owner, I want successful checks distinguished from capture dates, so that unchanged content can be recently verified without fabricated freshness.
40. As the owner, I want disappearance, source retirement, withdrawal and reinstatement distinguished, so that absence is not mistaken for nonexistence or distribution withdrawal.
41. As the owner, I want semantic drift diagnostics, so that meaningful coverage or identity changes stand out from cosmetic byte changes.
42. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want all published records in ordinary queries and exports, so that supplemental admission does not require special inclusion filters.
43. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want accepted facts and explicit unknowns without administrative evidence metadata, so that applications need not evaluate provenance to use the catalogue.
44. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want Printed Rules Text preserved alongside publisher-corrected content, so that corrections do not erase what appeared on a Printing.
45. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want Products, regional Releases and Distribution Contexts kept distinct, so that release groupings do not create false Printing identities.
46. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want role-labelled immutable Printing Images, so that multiple faces and backs can be consumed consistently.
47. As the owner, I want complete paginated candidate inspection, so that I can review every proposed entity, relationship, image and unknown.
48. As the owner, I want semantic before/after values and evidence-only changes, so that consequential changes cannot hide behind counts or lists of IDs.
49. As the owner, I want inspection pages pinned to one sealed candidate and predecessor, so that concurrent work cannot change what I am reviewing.
50. As the owner, I want whole-candidate approval without mandatory per-item acknowledgement, so that review remains practical while all details stay available.
51. As the owner, I want candidates prepared and approved independently per game, so that an unrelated game can progress without invalidating my review.
52. As the owner, I want approval to bind exact content and the game's predecessor, so that same-game changes cannot be silently rebased.
53. As the owner, I want bounded durable preparation with immutable image references, so that full catalogues do not require whole-catalogue buffers or oversized transactions.
54. As the owner, I want reconciliation and publication to return durable operation identities promptly, so that CLI timeouts do not define operation lifetimes.
55. As the owner, I want idempotent retries and inspectable status, so that a lost response cannot cause duplicate publication.
56. As the owner, I want exhausted transient retries to pause resumably, so that verified completed work is not discarded.
57. As the owner, I want superseded workers fenced, so that resume or abandonment cannot leave an old worker able to publish.
58. As the owner, I want the original seven-day candidate deadline enforced through approval and backup waits, so that stale review never becomes permanent approval.
59. As the owner, I want a correction's stated date preserved without scheduled activation, so that the catalogue publishes collected and reviewed facts rather than silently changing over time.
60. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want composition-pinned queries and pagination, so that concurrent game publications never mix versions within a view.
61. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want matching immutable Catalogue Exports, so that offline and API data describe the same published composition.
62. As a Catalogue Consumer, I want authenticated images, export range requests, conditional requests and stable problems, so that existing integrations remain practical.
63. As the owner, I want database-enforced publication guards, so that failed concurrency checks cannot expose partial staged data.
64. As the owner, I want a verified backup after each publication before the next, so that published progress does not outrun recovery.
65. As the owner, I want other games to prepare and receive approval while backup verification runs, so that the checkpoint delays only their final publication.
66. As the owner, I want global mutation fencing during actual Catalogue Recovery, so that restoration and new writes cannot undermine each other.
67. As the owner, I want bounded reference-aware cleanup, so that discarded staging work can be reclaimed without deleting shared evidence or recoverable data.
68. As the owner, I want evidence supporting published facts and owner decisions retained, so that those facts remain explainable.
69. As the owner, I want unused terminal work cleanup-eligible after 30 days, so that hypothetical future reparse does not justify indefinite storage.
70. As the owner, I want parser corrections to use fresh collection initially, so that launch does not depend on a cross-version reparse workflow.
71. As the owner, I want one real supplemental-only Printing verified against declared official coverage, so that supplemental admission is demonstrated with real evidence.
72. As the owner, I want actual Riftbound data to challenge the shared model, so that Bandai conventions do not become hidden universal assumptions.
73. As the owner, I want every enabled game to complete its real-source consumer journey twice, so that unsupported launch claims cannot hide behind another game's success.
74. As the owner, I want measured records, image bytes, memory, duration and amplification, so that capacity claims describe observed workloads.
75. As the owner, I want synthetic stress and fault cases labelled separately, so that a configured limit or successful guard is not mistaken for measured usable capacity.
76. As the owner, I want isolated dev, staging and production resources, so that tests and cleanup cannot mutate another environment.
77. As the owner, I want passing merges deployed automatically to dev, so that ongoing work is available for development checks.
78. As the owner, I want to select an exact commit manually for staging, so that a release begins deliberately rather than on every merge.
79. As the owner, I want successful staging validation to promote the same commit automatically, so that a second routine approval is unnecessary while release intent stays exact.
80. As the owner, I want newer merges unable to substitute for my selected release, so that production receives the software actually tested in staging.
81. As the owner, I want staging validation proportional to the change, so that routine changes do not require scraping every game again.
82. As the owner, I want routine production refreshes independent of software releases, so that catalogue approval remains the gate for data updates.
83. As the owner, I want exact-release-SHA CI and protected diagnostics, so that releases and failures are supported by meaningful evidence.
84. As the owner, I want environment-specific migration rehearsals, so that staging tests the production transition even when their catalogue data differs.
85. As the owner, I want a supported fresh-baseline handoff before Go-Live, so that final folding does not rely on manual ledger copying or deployment bypasses.
86. As the owner, I want generated release notes tied to the promoted commit, so that deployed changes remain traceable.
87. As the owner, I want all implementation and validation prerequisites complete before the explicit Go-Live call, so that planning completion cannot activate retained-version promises prematurely.

## Implementation Decisions

### Domain, authority and identity

- Publisher ownership, Source identity, Source Lineage, source transport permission and Source Authority are distinct. Authority is owner-designated by game and applicable card-fact/printing/corrected-content scope, locale and release region. No silent official-source takeover or outage fallback changes authority. Publisher-issued Errata remain attributable official corrections; manual corrections do not become publisher Errata.
- Each source adapter targets a shared typed Game Profile. Presentation changes belong in adapters; semantic changes require deliberate profile changes. Preserve optional unknown source values and actionable warnings. Keep required identity/structure checks strict. No dynamic plugin marketplace or universal untyped fact bag is required.
- Persistent opaque canonical IDs replace source-lineage/number/compatibility-derived identity. Store evidence-backed source aliases and mappings. Automatic matching requires an existing noncontradictory mapping or a game-specific rule identifying exactly one match. Number, name, similarity and identical downloaded bytes alone are insufficient. Missing numbers remain missing.
- A Printing represents an established issued distinction; mere distribution membership, manufacturing variance, changed image URL or re-encoding does not create one. Card equivalence and face/edition semantics are game-specific, including the unnumbered One Piece DON!! Card.
- Owner-reviewed merges retain a survivor and redirects; splits retire the conflated identity and link replacements without guessing consumer-owned variants. New published corrections preserve earlier Catalogue Revisions and exports. Recover mappings and admission/correction history with catalogue recovery.

### Admission, corrections and scope

- Game requirements define sufficient identity and required structure. Source rules specify acceptable evidence and automatic-admission permission without bypassing those requirements. A designated supplemental authority can automatically admit unambiguous records; other sources and manual intake require owner admission. There is no universal corroborating-source count.
- Entity Proposals retain unresolved intake outside published Catalogue Data and support admit/link/reject/reconsider with decision history. Automation cannot reverse an explicit owner rejection. Owner attestation and exceptions require recorded rationale/evidence and internally valid identity/structure. Existing-entity changes use Curated Revisions; new intake is a separate path.
- Stricter policy flags reassessment without automatic removal or ID churn. Material changes to overridden facts require owner reaffirmation, replacement or retirement; unrelated changes do not. An owner can reaffirm a disagreement explicitly without changing authority.
- Non-authoritative contradictions remain attributable warnings while selected authority governs; equal-authority conflicts require resolution. Isolate unresolved entities/scopes only when the remaining candidate is internally consistent, and disclose exclusions. Otherwise block. Later unambiguous official confirmation attaches to existing IDs and only confirms supported facts.
- Declare required/optional participation and complete source/subset coverage before collecting. Preserve successful captures from failed plans, but never relabel partial required capture as success. A narrower refresh must be explicit and independently complete. Optional outages carry prior accepted facts forward without fabricated verification dates.
- Preserve successful-check time separately from capture/content dates. Source retirement requires explicit authority/plan changes where applicable. Disappearance is a review signal; withdrawal and reinstatement need their own evidence and retain identity. Semantic drift distinguishes additions, cosmetic changes, coverage loss, identity changes and parser/profile faults.

### Content and contract replacement

- Replace the original Bandai-only/official-source-only, full-game-only, lineage-derived identity and supplemental-enrichment-only assumptions. The service remains private, authenticated and owner-operated; inventories, decks and other personal state belong to consumers.
- Remove tournament eligibility, Legality Rules, bans, organised-play restrictions, FAQs/rulings and their acquisition dependencies, projections, admission/publication gates, API/CLI surfaces, export components, tests, production smokes and freeze requirements together. Do not retain permanent unknown eligibility fields as a substitute. A mixed publisher page may still be acquired for its in-scope card correction evidence without acquiring a legality obligation.
- Retain Printed Rules Text, publisher-corrected content and Errata, Product/Release/Distribution Context facts, explicit in-scope unknowns, images, identity/history and recovery. Correction dates remain evidence; no scheduled activation, continuous monitoring or date-crossing candidate invalidation is required.
- Consumers receive accepted in-scope facts, meaningful catalogue lifecycle/correction relationships and explicit unknowns. Remove provenance sidecars, confirmation/confidence badges, source-health/freshness metadata, disagreements and source/admission filters from consumer API/exports. All published records appear normally. Administration retains the full evidence and source history.
- Replace live OpenAPI/JSON Schema, export serialization, CLI and administration contracts and their acceptance cases consistently. Reclassify superseded prototypes as historical decision references; their schemas/scenarios must not remain a competing normative contract. Preserve unrelated private-read, authenticated image/export, CORS, query ordering, conditional/range, stable-problem, guarded export deletion and recovery behavior.
- Before Go-Live change the single current definitions in place and regenerate incompatible derived data; do not maintain prelaunch legacy APIs/export schemas for compatibility. Temporary implementation sequencing is allowed only as bounded work with final removal, not a permanent second contract. Guard updates to existing environments and preserve operational evidence/recovery. From Go-Live retain immutable definition versioning under the amended ADRs. Cross-version reparse is explicitly deferred: a parser correction uses freshly captured evidence and ordinary candidate review. Existing same-version operations are not removed by this deferral.

### Bounded candidates and publication

- Use Workers/Workflows for entry points and bounded durable orchestration, R2 for immutable bytes/partitioned artifacts and D1 for operation state, query projections and the final guarded switch. Queues, Durable Objects or external compute are optional responses to demonstrated needs, not initial dependencies. Concurrent collectors share hostname pacing.
- Permit concurrent collection across sources and games; serialize reconciliation/review/publication per game, with one current candidate process per game while collection may continue. Pin exact observations, mappings, admission decisions, policies/profiles and owner corrections. Seal immutable candidate content and partitioned manifests before review; new evidence never silently changes it.
- Store image identities, immutable references, byte lengths, media types and digests outside bounded metadata. Partition records, relationships, evidence, diffs, export components and projection work. Do not replace the old image-bearing aggregate with a metadata-only whole-game buffer. Subdivide large entities/relationships or report explicit capacity failure; never truncate silently.
- Reconciliation and approval promptly return a durable operation identity/status location. Persist approval before acknowledgement. Exact idempotent intent returns the same operation/result; changed intent under the same key fails. Persist phases, progress, attempts and outcomes independently of transient Workflow history.
- Bounded transient retries lead to an inspectable pause; explicit resume reuses verified work. Integrity failures, stale predecessors and expiry are not indefinite transport retries. Ownership generations fence superseded/abandoned workers. Abandonment releases the game slot after fencing and preserves decision evidence.
- Whole-candidate approval binds its digest/identity and expected Game Catalogue Revision. Same-game predecessor changes require a new candidate and approval; another game's publication does not. The original seven-day deadline continues through approval, pauses, preparation and backup waits and is checked at final switch. Expiry requires fresh approval of a new candidate.
- Administration provides complete consistently pinned pages for candidate content and semantic before/after differences, images, all entity/relationship classes, identity/admission/correction decisions, warnings, exclusions, evidence-only changes, source coverage and actual verification dates. Summary counts reconcile with details. Missing/corrupt required artifacts block readiness. No per-item acknowledgement requirement or permanent review UI is introduced.
- Stage and verify objects, query/search projections and export artifacts before visibility. The final small database-enforced transaction validates readiness, exact approval, expected game predecessor, current composition, writer generation, deadline and recovery health; atomically advances composition, records success and reserves backup. A failed condition must prevent all sibling writes. No catalogue-sized work belongs inside this transaction.
- On unrelated-game contention rebuild only bounded composition references and retry while preserving exact approved game content/deadline. Never auto-rebase same-game content. API pagination/images/export references must observe consistent complete compositions, including replica/session behavior. Reuse immutable carry-forward and unrelated-game export components instead of regenerating them.
- Verify each published composition's backup through Disposable Restore before any subsequent publication. Other games may collect, prepare, inspect and receive durable approval during verification, but their final switches wait. Actual shared-database Catalogue Recovery remains globally fenced through verification and explicit acceptance. Restored snapshots cannot promise preservation of later pending work; classify/fence staging and operation state safely.

### Retention and initial engineering targets

- Retain source evidence supporting published facts and owner decisions, including evidence needed to explain historical publications and identity corrections. Removing consumer provenance does not authorize evidence deletion.
- Unused captures and abandoned work become cleanup-eligible 30 days after terminal completion. Treat this as adjustable and necessary but insufficient: verify no active/paused operation, decision, retained candidate, published history, export or recovery reference requires the material. Fence writers first, recheck eligibility before deletion, and persist bounded resumable cleanup intent/results. Respect storage multipart lifecycle constraints without treating them as permission to delete protected evidence. No retention solely for hypothetical cross-version reparse is required.
- Retain existing current-plus-two composition queryability and substantive backup/guarded export-retention protections. The new unused-evidence policy does not silently shorten export or recovery retention.

| Unit | Initial adjustable target |
| --- | --- |
| Metadata partition / admin metadata page | At most 1 MiB serialized and 500 records, whichever binds first |
| Peak isolate working set | At most 64 MiB under representative concurrency |
| Durable unit | Target at most 10 seconds CPU, 100 service calls, four concurrent object streams; finite wall-time/retry budgets |
| D1 staging batch | At most 100 mutations / 1 MiB bound data within statement limits; under one second p95 target, five-second operational ceiling |
| Final transaction | At most 20 statements / 64 KiB request payload; same latency target and no catalogue-sized work |
| Workflow shard | At most 1,000 planned steps / 5,000 planned service calls including retries and continuation |
| Export component | Independently addressable 8 MiB target; stream larger artifacts where required |
| D1 occupancy | Review topology before projected total exceeds 5 GB including indexes, retained data and permitted concurrent staging |
| Administration starts/status | Under two seconds p95 target within the existing ten-second CLI deadline, excluding streamed downloads |

These are accepted starting targets, not observed throughput, permanent schema limits, a monthly cost cap or a completion SLA. Record tuning and measure actual platform headroom and billed dimensions before making capacity/cost claims.

### Environments, release and freeze

- The complete isolated dev/staging/production flow is a Go-Live prerequisite. Each environment has separate catalogue and disposable-restore targets, evidence/object storage, Workflow namespaces, secrets and route configuration. Namespace inventory and cleanup before provisioning so one environment cannot delete another's scratch database. Verify account capacity and replacement-recovery headroom before creating resources; historical quota observations are not current proof.
- Automatically deploy a merge to dev after its exact-commit CI succeeds. Staging is not updated automatically on merge. An owner-initiated release selects an immutable exact commit and starts staging deployment and validation. Once required staging checks pass, automatically promote that same commit to production through live production guards. No second routine approval is required. A failed guard/check stops progression; a new merge never substitutes a commit.
- Preserve serialized guarded mutation, least-privilege credential separation, target/binding checks, schema state, recovery checks and stable release identity. Initiating staging expresses release intent; it does not waive later production validation. Use a bounded immutable promotion authorization and stage-specific fresh validation rather than forwarding an expired production confirmation or requiring an unplanned second human approval. Do not expose administration credentials to Actions or deployment credentials to the CLI merely to simplify orchestration; changes to that boundary require explicit architectural review.
- Staging uses its own catalogue operations and isolated data. Test software changes against retained real-source fixtures and proportionate live validation; full rehearsals are mandatory before Go-Live and for major ingestion/publication/recovery changes. Record the selected validation scope with the release and make the required result enforceable. Routine production catalogue refreshes do not require staging and retain production candidate approval.
- Stage software and compatible migrations against the production transition's actual recorded starting schema level. Independent staging data may differ, but an already-upgraded staging database is not proof of the migration production will execute. Preserve compatibility throughout activation, and stop/revalidate if production target/schema guards become stale. Do not copy staging data over production or introduce interpretation/evidence transfer as publication.
- Require complete expected CI checks on the exact deployed SHA, not a merged PR's earlier head; reject missing, pending or failed shards. Restore runner availability if unavailable. Historical successful local gates cannot waive the release gate. Preserve useful bounded/redacted cause diagnostics tied to requests and durable operations without leaking credentials, source payloads or sensitive internals to consumers.
- Generate release notes/changelog for the exact promoted revision; release metadata is not a bypass around manual staging initiation. Existing draft rollout work is prior art and must be reconciled with these triggers and expanded semantics.
- Implement the supported fresh-baseline authority handoff through the old runtime before final baseline folding. Refresh the fold/proof after all schema-changing work; preserve frozen identifier suffixes unless the owner explicitly changes that existing choice. Do not use direct deployment or manual ledger copying as a cutover shortcut. Rehearse final cutover, obtain exact-release-SHA CI and live recovery/retention evidence, then require the separate owner Go-Live declaration. Mark actual dates only when Go-Live happens. Cross-version reparse is not a freeze gate.

## Testing Decisions

The owner confirmed the existing CLI plus authenticated API boundary as the primary acceptance seam. Exercise locally emulated production Workers through real public administration/consumer interfaces; assert observable facts, operation outcomes, errors, pagination and retained history. Prefer this seam to tests coupled to private modules, SQL layouts or workflow decomposition. Focused parser, serializer or transaction tests may supplement it where a failure cannot be established efficiently at the system boundary; they do not replace end-to-end proof.

Prior art includes the existing game catalogue, source-evidence, candidate/publication, Errata, Curated Revision, backup/restore, release-gate, schema-baseline and operational-diagnostics acceptance suites, real official-source parser fixtures and deterministic export golden cases. Revise obsolete scenarios rather than preserving superseded legality/provenance/locking requirements as assertions.

### Required evidence and replay matrix

| Area | Required proof |
| --- | --- |
| One Piece across Bandai and Limitless | Retain dated raw responses, relevant headers, digests and image evidence for complete declared English source coverage; verify at least one same-Printing match across sources and one genuine supplemental-only Printing against an explicit bounded official scope. P-001's seven-versus-eight counts and distribution wording alone do not prove equivalence or absence. |
| New Card admission | Label synthetic supplemental-only Card, missing identifier, later confirmation and conflict scenarios explicitly. Include a verified real supplemental-only Card if found; finding one is not a launch gate. Owner-attested evidence remains available under admission policy. |
| Riftbound | Retain actual official gallery data and publisher correction evidence; challenge number/alias formats, treatment and face semantics, release facts and Printed/Effective Rules Text. Unknown faces and placeholders remain unknown. Quantify declared coverage; the earlier sample is not a complete inventory. |
| Existing game regressions | Replay Fusion World base/alternate records together through identity and candidate behavior; preserve optional unknown Digimon mechanics with warnings while malformed required structure fails. Exercise applicable DON!!, regional and multi-face semantics for each enabled game. |
| Identity/admission | Same-Printing cross-source mapping, ambiguous matches, missing numbers, image URL/re-encoding, merge/split references, exceptions, proposal rejection/reconsideration, changed-policy reassessment, override reaffirmation and later confirmation preserving IDs. Restore identity mappings and history. |
| Coverage | Required failure, optional outage, 99-of-100 capture, explicit narrower retry, no-change verification, supplemental carry-forward, disappearance, retirement, withdrawal/reinstatement and semantic drift. Never claim omitted scopes were checked. |
| Inspection/consumer contract | All entity/relationship changes including product-only, release-only, image-only and evidence-only differences; complete pinned pages, counts and inspectable images; ordinary supplemental visibility; API/export parity; explicit in-scope unknowns; absence of removed eligibility and consumer evidence surfaces. |
| Durable operations | Full/no-change/incremental refresh, high-degree entities, interrupted boundaries, duplicate/lost requests, bounded retry exhaustion/resume, stale writer fencing, supersession/abandonment, expiry after approval and during backup waits, corruption, partial staging and reference-safe cleanup. |
| Composition and recovery | Same-game stale approval, unrelated-game publication contention without lost updates, consistent reads/pagination/exports, backup failure/retry, actual restore and global fencing. A correction date crossing without new evidence neither recomputes nor invalidates approval. |
| Release | Green PR head with red merge, missing/pending shards, exact-SHA success, no staging-on-merge, selected-commit pinning across newer merges, staging failure blocking production, automatic production after valid staging, changed production guards, environment-scoped cleanup and migration rehearsal from the correct starting state. |
| Retention/diagnostics | Thirty-day eligibility boundaries; paused/shared/published/decision/recovery evidence protected; cleanup interrupted/retried safely. Unexpected API/ingestion failures preserve redacted cause correlation and never leak secrets or bodies. |

For each game enabled for Catalogue Consumers, demonstrate the complete real-source journey twice: collect, reconcile, inspect, approve, browse/search, image delivery, offline export verification and verified recovery, including a subsequent refresh. Cover both changed and no-change behavior across the replay matrix. Keep unsupported games disabled until their evidence passes. Validate the One Piece two-source case and actual second publisher before freezing shared contracts; a bounded case must never be reported as all cards in a game.

Retain executable replay assets, capture metadata and expected outcomes; the original research dossier contains concise observations and a response digest, not complete retained raw fixtures. Record real findings separately from injected faults, provider claims and hypotheses. If the required genuine supplemental-only Printing or declared coverage cannot be established, report a failed evidence gate rather than inventing a match or silently replacing it with synthetic data.

### Capacity and operational proof

1. Eliminate the reproduced 128 images × 100 KiB rejection case through the actual pipeline. The historical 17,526,322-byte candidate failure is a reproduced guard failure, not a measured complete-game ingest.
2. Exercise synthetic workloads of 10,000 Printings / 20,000 images / 5 GiB image bytes / 100 MiB structured data, and 100,000 Printings / 200,000 images / 50 GiB image bytes / 1 GiB structured data. Explicitly distinguish successful usable capacity from correct guard-triggering rejection.
3. Measure complete declared One Piece two-source and actual second-publisher workloads: request/record/image counts, source and retained bytes, metadata/export bytes, peak working set, CPU and wall time, service calls, rows/index/write amplification, retained/concurrent storage, billed dimensions and owner actions. Do not substitute configured request limits for census data.
4. Derive completion/cost targets from recorded measurements and revise adjustable budgets transparently. No measured throughput, cost ceiling or SLA is asserted by this specification.
5. Verify backup through isolated restore and representative API/invariant checks. Rehearse interruption and recovery and final release/cutover; do not infer recoverability from object existence or green unit tests.

## Out of Scope

- Original/custom cards, community submissions/moderation, public/anonymous/multi-tenant API access, inventories/decks/trading/prices and non-English ingestion.
- Tournament eligibility, ban lists, organised-play restrictions, FAQs/rulings and permanent unknown eligibility projections.
- A permanent administration UI, generated review UI requirement, unrestricted adapter marketplace or mandatory new queue/coordination platform.
- Cross-version reparse at Go-Live, indefinite evidence retention solely for that possibility, staging-to-production catalogue copying or parsed-evidence promotion.
- Mandatory staging runs for routine catalogue refreshes on unchanged software; mandatory full-game re-scraping for every small software change.
- Automatic authority changes, scheduled card-correction activation, multi-game atomic publication, silent same-game approval rebasing or weakened recovery gates.
- New external disaster-recovery guarantees, public compatibility promises or prelaunch legacy definition retention. Existing operational protections remain.
- Production provisioning, mutation or Go-Live authorization by virtue of this planning/specification issue being created or closed.

## Further Notes

This is the replacement implementation specification for [Decision map: evolve Card Keepr across publishers and sources](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/207), including the owner-confirmed [Decide validation, contract revisions, and specification handoff](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/215). It supersedes conflicting requirements in [Implement the personal Bandai card catalogue and API](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/22); unrelated existing behavior remains unless explicitly replaced above. Earlier decision references to legality, consumer provenance and temporal activation must be read through the later scope/publication decisions.

The detailed decision trail is indexed by the map: [source authority](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/209#issuecomment-5555935244), [identity](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/210#issuecomment-5556048893), [admission](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/211#issuecomment-5556519627), [coverage](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/212#issuecomment-5557581630), [consumer visibility and inspection](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/213#issuecomment-5558597280), [card-content scope](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/214#issuecomment-5558719187) and [durable publication](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/214#issuecomment-5558801899).

The review baseline was `60415d00da0ccbc843eb92d0c8f6545dd15271c4`. The original working checkout is older and has unrelated edits; implementation must begin from a verified current baseline rather than repeating completed restructuring. Reproduced Fusion World, image-budget and optional-Digimon-field defects are distinct from inspected synchronous-publication/inspection/diagnostic/release-gate paths and the now-deferred reparse promise gap. CI availability must be rechecked; historical runner failures are not application-test failures.

[Automated environment promotion: dev and staging environments, changelog generation, and hands-off production deployment](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/151) remains the existing rollout initiative and must adopt the selected manual-staging/automatic-production flow. Its draft work is reusable prior art, not a completed rollout. [Go-Live freeze: fold migrations into the baseline and start version retention](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/136) remains blocked by this specification's implementation, validation, full environment rollout and supported fresh-baseline handoff. Existing draft fold/proof work must be refreshed after those schema changes. [Backlog map: close every open ticket before Go-Live](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/155) remains historical execution context; its former two-ticket launch checkpoint is superseded.

Implementation tickets will be reviewed as independently verifiable vertical slices and linked by native dependencies before publication. This specification does not mark implementation complete, restore CI, establish real-source equivalence/capacity, provision environments or approve Go-Live.
